PLAN 211.title: City-Making: A Global Perspective
PLAN 211.description: Contemporary city development trends, policies, and practices across the globe as explored against the backdrop of culture and technology. Includes hands-on learning.

PLAN 221.title: City Visuals
PLAN 221.description: An exploratory journey through the vast world of visualizing the city and ways of representing the built environment, including how to both interpret and use visualizations to read the city.

prerequisite.raw: Second-year standing or above in any program

PLAN 221.prerequisiteText: Second-year standing or above in any program

PLAN 231.title: Methods of Community Engagement
PLAN 231.description: Examination of various approaches to hands-on engagement with urban communities while examining the meaning of public, community, and participation.

PLAN 321.title: Indigeneity and the City
PLAN 321.description: Place-based exploration of the multiple, complex and contested ways urban Indigeneity is constituted in Canada today, with opportunities for field trips and hands-on learning.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 321.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 331.title: The Just City in a Divided World
PLAN 331.description: Considers the city as a terrain for the manifestation and mediation of social justice. Explores how the allocation of land, goods, and services in cities (re)produces social stratification, and how institutions and civil society negotiate just and unjust outcomes.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 331.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 341.title: Smart Cities: Concepts, Methods and Design
PLAN 341.description: Rapid transformation of cities by information technology and socio-economic innovation; growth in citizen-generated data and the internet of things; emerging theory, methods, and frameworks for understanding Smart Cities.

prerequisite.raw: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second-year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 341.prerequisiteText: Third-year standing or above in any program. Second-year students may be admitted with permission of instructor

PLAN 351.title: Green Cities
PLAN 351.description: The key social and technological challenges, contradictions, and opportunities in planning for ecologically sound urbanization.

PLAN 352.title: Planning for Urban Climate and Energy Transitions
PLAN 352.description: Urban planning approaches to mitigating and adapting to climate change with a focus on local-level energy system transitions.

PLAN 361.title: Community Planning in a World of Diversity
PLAN 361.description: Examination of how the diverse, multicultural, and cosmopolitan aspects of cities create challenges and opportunities for community planning.

PLAN 372.title: Urban Housing Justice and Planning
PLAN 372.description: Critical overview of urban housing systems and policy tools for housing justice.

PLAN 425.title: Urban Planning Issues and Concepts
PLAN 425.description: Evolution, practice and future of urban planning and development, with emphasis on institutional arrangements, housing, transportation, urban design and development control. For third- and fourth-year undergraduate students interested in urban planning. .

PLAN 452.title: Urban Studies Capstone II
PLAN 452.description: Application of key elements of urban studies theory, concepts, and methods to a community-engaged urban challenge.

PLAN 461.title: Planning for Health Equity
PLAN 461.description: The role of urban planning and policy in producing social and environmental conditions for health equity. Restricted to students in the Bachelor of Arts Major in Urban Studies with at least fourth-year standing.

PLAN 500.title: Comparative Perspectives on Planning History and Futures

PLAN 508.title: Foundations of Planning Theory and History

PLAN 509.title: Urbanism as a Global Way of Life

PLAN 510.title: Environment and Sustainability Concepts for Planning Practice

PLAN 511.title: The Legal and Institutional Context of Planning

PLAN 512.title: Urban Economics, Infrastructure, and Real Estate Issues in Planning

PLAN 513.title: Making and Implementing Community and Regional Plans

PLAN 514.title: Indigenous Planning: Ways of Being, Knowing and Doing

PLAN 515.title: Indigenous Law, Governance and Community Planning

PLAN 517.title: Theory and Methods of Urban Design
PLAN 517.description: Application of urban design theory to a neighbourhood design.

PLAN 526.title: Selected Topics in Experimental Learning: The Planning Studio

PLAN 530.title: Affordable Housing Policy and Planning
PLAN 530.description: The history of housing and homelessness policies as well as current issues and challenges faced by municipalities, regional governments, non-profit housing providers, and others.

PLAN 531.title: Planning for Disaster-Resilient Communities
PLAN 531.description: Natural disasters from the perspective of risk analysis, risk reduction, and planning for disaster-resilient communities. Focus primarily on Canada and the U.S. but includes disaster risk globally.

PLAN 532.title: Strategic Planning: Developing and Implementing Policy Plans
PLAN 532.description: Theory and practice of developing and implementing plans for sustainable regions, cities, and neighbourhoods. Combining land use, transportation, environment, socio-economic, and financial directions, managing plan making including public participation, and writing council reports.

PLAN 534.title: Introduction to Geographic Information Systems
PLAN 534.description: Theory, history and capabilities behind GIS, with customized laboratory exercises that incorporate urban design and planning themes.

PLAN 535.title: Transportation Planning & Analysis
PLAN 535.description: Foundations of urban travel modelling: data needs; survey and sampling techniques; model calibration and validation; discrete choice modeling; 4-step travel demand forecasting (trip generation, distribution, modal choice, and assignment); activity based models; integrated land use/transport models.

PLAN 542.title: Practical Practice: City Planning as a Craft
PLAN 542.description: Approach, role, style, and essential skills of practical urban planning: working at the community level; developing overall policy; managing development; undertaking urban design; and engaging in the political process.

PLAN 545.title: Planning Studies Abroad
PLAN 545.description: An extended site visit outside Canada to understand the cultural context for community and regional planning issues and the local institutional response.

PLAN 548.title: Current Issues in Planning
PLAN 548.description: Each year the school may offer one or more courses on a topical issue covering recent advances in the field.

PLAN 549.title: Master's Thesis
PLAN 549.description: Research and preparation of a thesis on a topic in public policy or professional practice.

PLAN 550.title: Directed Studies
PLAN 550.description: Students must contact the department for permission to register. Pass/Fail.

PLAN 558.title: The Role of Theory in Planning Research
PLAN 558.description: This course will be taken in the first term of the Master's program.

PLAN 559.title: Design of Planning- and Policy-Oriented Research
PLAN 559.description: Research design for SCARP thesis-based Master's students. Approaches for designing research methodologies and thesis structure. Selection processes for research focus; linking research problems to methodological sources; logics of structuring the thesis.

PLAN 565.title: Current Issues in Real Property Development and Planning

PLAN 579.title: Public Health, Transportation, and the Built Environment
PLAN 579.description: Health issues associated with transportation and the built environment; design of urban form for non-motorized transportation for the improvement of personal and environmental health; factors that impact transportation choices; applying findings from research to specific transportation planning processes and projects.

PLAN 580.title: Urban Transportation Planning
PLAN 580.description: Topics include the relationship between transportation and urban activity systems; analysis of supply and demand; accessibility and environment; institutional arrangements and public finance.

PLAN 583.title: Housing and Community Planning Policy
PLAN 583.description: Homes and communities are a focus of public policy for local and senior governments. Overview of past and current policies addressing the design and development of homes and communities.

PLAN 587.title: Urban Design
PLAN 587.description: A studio/seminar on the history of the physical form of cities and theories of city design. Topics include social impacts, heritage and environmental conservation, urban revitalization, and the legal and administrative instruments for the implementation of city designs.

PLAN 591.title: Land Use and Environmental Policy
PLAN 591.description: Identify potential impacts of human land use activities on environmental systems; review policies in place at various levels of government in Canada (and elsewhere) that promote sustainable development and reduce negative impacts; assess effectiveness of those policies; design new policies.

PLAN 597.title: Planning for Water Resources Management
PLAN 597.description: The relationships among relevant bio-physical, socio-economic and institutional systems as applied to regional planning for watersheds, lakes, estuaries, coastal zones and international river basins. Water supply, waste disposal, fisheries, aquaculture, recreation, hydropower and flood control.
